title: First-Class Appendices for Print Reports and Zwischenbericht Anhänge
description: Add first-class appendix support to the semio print system (print/tex/): an appendix is a document attached to the main report, behaving like a chapter — numbered A, B, C…, labeled Anhang/Appendix, TOC entry, chip styling, cross-referenceable via \appendixref, listed via \listofappendices. Fix a pre-existing bug where window registers (\listoffigures etc.) render header-only because semio@render@register reads the wrong body macro. Wire the feature into all six print templates (report, paper, flyer n/a, zukunftbau forschungsbericht/zwischenbericht/kompaktbericht). Then apply it to mit-bestand/bericht/zwischenbericht/zwischenbericht.tex: convert 9 Anhang markdown documents from temp/ into 8 LaTeX appendices (A-H), including a 67-project table with per-row avatar images sourced from temp/projekt_bilder/ (downscaled ~600px, copied into zwischenbericht/asset/projekt/). Update body cross-references to use \appendixref. Full plan at /Users/ueli/.claude/plans/print-reports-should-be-joyful-haven.md.
summary:
Every appendix and appendix-chapter can now declare its own semantic identifier prefix instead of the automatic A, B, C… (`\appendixchapter[H]{Hürden}`, `\appendixsection[DG]{...}` → composed as `H`, `I-DG`), with compile-time duplicate-identifier detection (`\g_semio_appendix_ids_prop`) and numeric fallbacks when no prefix is given. Implemented via expandable indirection installed once into `\the<level>`/`\the<child level>` (`\semio_appendix_id:n`, `\semio_appendix_child_id:nn`) so every existing consumer (labels, hierarchy-path chip numbering, TOC, appendix register) picks up prefixes automatically; `\theH<level>` stays purely counter-based for stable hyperref destinations. All 6 print templates updated to the new `\appendixchapter[prefix]{title}` / `\appendixinput[prefix]{title}{file}` / new `\appendixsection[prefix]{title}` signatures, demonstrating both prefixed and Alph-fallback appendices.

Applied the full prefix map to the zwischenbericht: P Projekte (P-K/P-Q), H Hürden, BB Bauteilbörsen (BB-M/D/V/R/B/L), SB Sekundärbefunde (SB-B/Q), I Interviews — merged the three separate interview appendices into one with child chapters I-DG/I-KW/I-T — US User Stories und Anforderungsmapping, V Verzeichnisse. Fully integrated the scheme into every in-table identifier carried from the source markdown: Bauteilbörsen platform IDs `[P8]`→`BB-08` (100 occurrences), Hürden rows `1`–`13`→`H-01`–`H-13`, User Story IDs `BB-01`/`A-01`/`T-01`/`E-01`→`US-BB-01`/`US-A-01`/`US-T-01`/`US-E-01` (35 headings + 17 mapping-table cells).

Found and fixed a real bug during final verification: `\semio_register_list_reset:` (semio-window.sty) wrapped `\semio@register@listfalse` inside `\group_begin:`/`\group_end:`, so the assignment was immediately undone when the group closed — `\ifsemio@register@list` stayed stuck `true` forever after the first `\SemioTableLong`-based table (used by Projekte's Katalog/Quellen and by Bauteilbörsen) closed. Every heading after that silently lost its chip (`\semio@if@heading@chips` took the no-chip branch) and the hierarchy-path chip numbering for all subsequent windows went stale (e.g. the Hürden table showed "Tabelle: P-K.a" instead of "Tabelle: H.a"). Root-caused via two isolated tectonic reproductions (bisected: two plain `\appendixsection`s were fine, one `\SemioTableLong` reproduced it), fixed by replacing the grouped assignment with `\use:c { semio@register@listfalse }` (mirroring how the true-setter already worked, csname-based, no group). Rebuilt and re-verified all 6 print templates and the full zwischenbericht (light+dark): every appendix and sub-chapter chip renders correctly (P, P-K, P-Q, H, BB+6 sub-chapters, SB+2, I-DG/I-KW/I-T with deep `.1`–`.7` numbering, US+3), zero unresolved references, zero compile errors.
